Dynamic Response Study of Block-Type Machine Foundations with Integrated Geomaterial Layers

Abstract:

Machine-induced vibrations can significantly affect the performance, safety, and service life of foundations and supporting equipment. Block-type machine foundations are widely used in industrial applications however, their dynamic response is strongly influenced by soil&ndashstructure interaction and the properties of the supporting soil. Incorporating engineered geomaterial layers offers a promising approach to reducing vibration transmission and improving foundation performance.

This research investigates the dynamic response of block-type machine foundations integrated with geomaterial layers using finite element analysis in ANSYS. A three-dimensional machine&ndashfoundation&ndashsoil model is developed to simulate harmonic loading while considering soil&ndashstructure interaction. The study will evaluate the effects of different geomaterial layers on displacement, acceleration, stress distribution, natural frequency, and vibration attenuation. The performance of foundations with integrated geomaterial layers will be compared with that of conventional foundations to assess their effectiveness in vibration control. Further to that parametric study of results for non-reinforced and reinforced (By using Geomaterial) soil obtained from numerical model will be revalidated with experimental results. The outcomes are expected to provide practical design recommendations for developing efficient, durable, and vibration-resistant machine foundation systems.
